Samantha — thanks, great questions. Short answers up front, followed by next steps and an attachment: a 1-page runbook summary and a DPA addendum draft (attached).

1) Region pinning: yes — we support account-level pinning to US / EU / APAC. When pinning is enabled, production inference requests are routed to the pinned region by default.

2) Transient egress (failover / capacity events): we allow short, controlled transient processing in a secondary region under defined conditions (regional outage, operator-driven maintenance, or customer-authorized temporary scaling). Our proposed maximum window is 72 hours for unplanned failover; anything longer requires explicit approval documented in the SOW or DPA addendum. All transient hops are recorded with start/end timestamps and request-level telemetry for audit.

3) Auditability & keys: every transient event emits an audit record to the tenant's audit log; if a customer uses their own KMS keys, keys remain in the primary region and are not exported — we only process encrypted payloads in secondary regions for the transient window unless otherwise agreed.

4) Subprocessors: current roster for your account attached in the runbook sheet; we can provide a live roster export for procurement. Any planned subprocessor addition with impact to residency will be communicated 30 days in advance to your security contact.

Attachments: DPA_Addendum_CardinalHealth_Sept2026.pdf (DPA addendum draft), residency-runbook-summary.xlsx (runbook + subprocessor sheet)

Next steps I propose: legal review of the DPA addendum (Marissa), ops validation of the runbook (Irene), and then we deliver an executed addendum via DocuSign for procurement. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to walk through the exact failover language.

— Mateo

Hi Samantha — looping in legal / contracts for explicit language. Mateo's draft covers the intent; below are the exact edits Legal requests for the addendum before we pass to procurement: 

- Define the transient egress "trigger conditions" (regional outage, scheduled maintenance if customer opted into maintenance window, or explicit customer request).
- Cap transient egress to a maximum of 72 continuous hours without written customer approval; allow for a single 72-hour extension only with signed change order.
- Require that Redwood provide a signed incident report and audit export within 5 business days after any transient egress event. Audit export must include request-level timestamps, region of processing, and operator justification.
- For KMS-managed keys: clarify that customer-managed keys remain region-bound and that any processing in a secondary region will be performed on ciphertext unless customer authorizes key rewrap/replication in writing.
- Subprocessor additions: Redwood will notify Cardinal Health 30 calendar days prior to activation of any subprocessor that could materially affect residency; allow for procurement to request a 45-day review period for high-risk subprocessors.

Irene, please confirm the feasibility of the 5-business-day audit deliverable and the operational tagging we need to surface in your telemetry exports.

If those items are acceptable, we'll incorporate the edits and send the DocuSign package.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference
